description.narrative:
The Center for Social Impact Studies (CeSIS) and the Savanna Research and Advocacy Network (SRAN) seek to build the capacity of communities affected by the operations of multinational extractive companies to effectively negotiate arrangements that can secure their livelihoods. The organizations also undertake initiatives aimed at ensuring policy change in favour of communities affected by miningoperations. SRAN and CeSIS also engage with diverse stakeholders to design various livelihood interventions formarginalized communities affected by the operations of extractive companies in Ghana. In an era where digitization and going green have become topical, the issue of sustainability has become even more compelling; especially for organisations whose ultimate goal is impact and not profit. Sustaining projects and programmes in this context become a herculean task, especially,when the project’s funding cycle ends. Projects which require continuity are sometimes left without fully harnessing their impacts. This, chiefly, boils down to resource mobilization, lack of strategic planning, and a host of other challenges which need to be traversed with innovation and tactfulness.
In view of this, CeSIS is partnering with SRAN to identify these organizational challenges that have ripple effects on the sustainability of projects, and require capacity strengthening to enhance shared benefits between the two organizations.
Project Description and Activities The Sustainable Organizations Project (SOP) is focused on strengthening the institutional capacity of CeSIS and SRAN . The project seeks to bridge organizational lapses and challenges identified through Needs Assessment Meetings, and to empower the organizations to ensure sustainable projects that harness their full potential and impacts.
Activity 1 Resource mobilization (Fundraising) – This activity goes to the core of the sustainability of the PVP intervention and future projects of the two organizations. The organizations will explore an exchange learning of practical and viable ways of raising funds. Knowledge acquired will be used to design a Fundraising Action Plan for implementation. Knowledge and learning exchange of the post implementation of the Fundraising Action Plan will be organized for the two organizations to learn from each other their successes, challenges, and how to navigate the challenges going forward.
Activity 2 Strategic planning – This will be a strategic planning session to develop a 5 year development plan for the two organisations. This is essential to the organizations’ sustainability because it will guide in decision-making and allocation of resources for the progress of projects. Knowledge gained from this session will be used to develop a 5-year strategic plan for each organisation.
Activity 3 Develop gender-based tools like gender budgeting and gender analysis. This will promote inclusiveness in project design and planning.
Activity 4 Develop a Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL)framework – This frameworkwill be used to monitor and evaluate programmes that the two organisations undertake in order to increase knowledge and learning. The MEL framework will support the sustainability of the organisations.
Activity 5 Training on Advocacy skills – This isa capacity building training workshop where both organisations will learn and share experiences in advocacy skills to enable them influencepolicy change in favour of their communities.

participating-org.narrative:
The Centre for Social Impact Studies (CeSIS) is a Non-governmental Organisation that seeks to influence policy change in favour of communities impacted by the operations of extractive companies. Established in January 2011 as an independent, not-for-profit, research and advocacy non-governmental organization, CeSIS primarily focused is on providing research backbone to Ghana’s extractive industry. CeSIS is headquartered in Obuasi in the Ashanti Region with an office in Takoradi, the Western Regional capital that focuses on the oil and gas industry. Officials of CeSIS have also travelled around the world sharing the organization’s experiences with students, researchers, civil society actors, government officials, and the business community. Vision CeSIS seeks to become a world class research institution providing cutting edge science based research results that support advocacy for the development of residents living in resource-rich areas in Ghana and Africa.
Mission CeSIS’s mission is to influence policy change in favour of communities impacted by the operations of extractive companies. This has been tremendously executed as CeSIS has become the sole mouthpiece of mining affected communities in Obuasi and adjoining districts especially on compensation, environmental and human rights issues.
Objectives CeSIS seeks to empower communities impacted by the operations of extractive companies for sustainable development of the extractive industry through advocacy, training and research. The Key specific objectives of CeSIS are to: I. Conduct research into the impact of extractive activities on communities impacted by the operations of extractive companies; II. Conduct research into specificissues as and when they are referred to the CeSIS by corporate bodies and other CSOs; III. Carry out advocacy activities for communities impacted by the operations of extractive companies using science based research results; IV. Push for policy change in the extractive industry in favour of the poor and marginalised communities; V. Promote the poor and marginalised communities participation in the co-management of Ghana extractive industry at all level of governance; VI. Educate residents of communities impacted by the operations of extractive companieson extractive industry related issues that affect their development, climate change, food security and socioeconomic wellbeing issues; and VII. Build the capacities of residents of communities impacted by the operations of extractive companies in entrepreneurial skills development to promote sustainable livelihood and food security
